Messages.Author: ALEX HARMON
Messages.Body:
Hi I was hoping some of the rulemongers could help out with a question here.

The Scenario:

I play a Haven Uncovered on Sir Walter.

My minion Demaskenos attacks Sir Walter (who is tapped) via Haven Uncovered.

My opponent plays a wake with evening's freshness and then an Obedience
to get out of combat. (at the time Sir Walter was older than my minion)

Question: is this legal? I argued that the Obedience card could only be
used if attempting to block something which he did not do since he needed
a +1 intercept. My opponent contended that Obedience stated "when about
to enter combat" and so therefore he could use it. Who is correct?

Messages.Author: Faethor
Messages.Body:
>My minion Demaskenos attacks Sir Walter (who is tapped) via Haven Uncovered.

Wait. Haven Uncovered reads, in part 'Put this card on any ready
vampire.' Yet you played it on a tapped vampire..? Is 'ready' being
used to indicate 'controlled'? What if the vampire is in Torpor?

-j

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:



Tapped has no bearing on ready status of a minion.

There are two regions: Controlled and Uncontrolled.
There are two areas in the Controlled region: Ready and Torpor.

Ready means in the ready area.

Messages.Author: Steve Bucy
Messages.Body:
Faethor <fae...@winternet.com> wrote:
>
>>My minion Demaskenos attacks Sir Walter (who is tapped) via Haven Uncovered.
>
> Wait. Haven Uncovered reads, in part 'Put this card on any ready
>vampire.' Yet you played it on a tapped vampire..? Is 'ready' being
>used to indicate 'controlled'? What if the vampire is in Torpor?

Controlled means any vampire you have in play (torpor, or active region).
Ready means any vampire in your active region (tapped or untapped). Thus
you can put Haven Uncovered on any vamp in the active region, but not on
a vamp in torpor.

Steve Bucy

Messages.Body:

>My minion Demaskenos attacks Sir Walter (who is tapped) via Haven Uncovered.

>My opponent plays a wake with evening's freshness and then an Obedience

>to get out of combat. (at the time Sir Walter was older than my minion)

>Question: is this legal? I argued that the Obedience card could only be
>used if attempting to block something which he did not do since he needed
>a +1 intercept. My opponent contended that Obedience stated "when about
>to enter combat" and so therefore he could use it. Who is correct?

Yes, it's legal. Your opponent is correct.

Obedience says nothing about blocking - only entering combat. It can
be used after a block, or after a successful Rush (provided the Rushee
is untapped).

Messages.Author: Michael Kelly
Messages.Body:
Faethor wrote:
>
> >My minion Demaskenos attacks Sir Walter (who is tapped) via Haven Uncovered.
>

> Wait. Haven Uncovered reads, in part 'Put this card on any ready
> vampire.' Yet you played it on a tapped vampire..? Is 'ready' being
> used to indicate 'controlled'? What if the vampire is in Torpor?
>

> -j
A vampire is controlled if it is flipped over and in play (either in the
ready region or in topor)

A vampire is ready if it is controlled and not in topor.

A vampire may be tapped or untapped while in topor or in the ready region.

So HU can be played on a tapped or untapped vampire in the ready region. It
can not be played on an uncontrolled vampire or one in topor.
